How a Debt Settlement
Lawyer Can Help You Reclaim Control

Are you struggling with mounting bills, collection calls, or fearing legal action from creditors? You’re not alone, and there are solutions. Many Iowans fall behind on payments due to medical emergencies, job loss, divorce, or the rising cost of living. The stress can feel overwhelming, but you don’t have to face it alone.

A debt settlement lawyer can help when the pressure becomes too much. Unlike credit counselors or debt relief companies, we provide legal protection while negotiating to reduce your debt, often saving you thousands of dollars. We handle creditors and collectors on your behalf, working to resolve unsecured debts like credit cards, personal loans, medical bills, and old judgments for a fraction of what you owe.

At Henkels & Baker PC, we know how debt can impact financial stability and peace of mind. With decades of experience and strong ties to Iowa, we have helped individuals and families break free from overwhelming debt and create a path toward financial recovery. We provide clear strategies and practical legal solutions, whether dealing with wage garnishments or struggling to make payments.

Practice Areas

Bankruptcy

  • Foreclosure
  • Wage Garnishment
  • Chapter 7 Bankruptcy

Debt Relief

  • Debt Settlement
  • Stop Creditor Harassment

Understanding Your Debt Settlement Options

Financial problems can feel overwhelming, affecting your job, relationships, and peace of mind. However, Iowa law offers options to help you regain control. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we assist Iowans in Dubuque and across the state by negotiating debt relief through legal settlements while protecting your rights under Iowa consumer laws and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA).

Debt settlement involves negotiating with creditors, like credit card companies, hospitals, or collection agencies, to reduce the amount you owe. Although Iowa doesn’t have a specific law for debt settlement, several laws shape this process, including:

  • Iowa Code § 537.7103: This law prevents creditors from using harassment, coercion, or false information to collect debts.

  • Iowa Code § 537.5201: This legal provision prohibits unfair or unreasonable terms in consumer credit contracts.

  • The FDCPA: Limits third-party debt collector behavior and allows you to dispute or verify debts.

Unlike national debt relief companies, our attorneys provide tailored, legally sound representation. We draft enforceable agreements, send legal demand letters to stop harassment, and ensure creditors follow Iowa’s consumer protection laws. By involving us, you reduce the chances of lawsuits or wage garnishment, which Iowa law (Iowa Code § 642.21) allows up to 25% of disposable income.

Debt settlement is more than reducing your debt—it protects your financial future. We use the law to safeguard your rights and guide you every step of the way.

Why Choose an Iowa Debt Settlement Attorney?

Dealing with overwhelming debt can be stressful, but having the right attorney can make all the difference. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we provide real solutions, not empty promises. We tailor our legal strategies to your debt situation and financial goals, using Iowa law to help you achieve lasting financial recovery.

The Advantage of Local Legal Experience

National debt settlement companies often rely on generic, one-size-fits-all solutions. As Iowa-based attorneys, we use our deep understanding of Iowa law, including Iowa Code Chapters 537 and 642, to protect your rights and assets.

Our local knowledge allows us to:

  • Spot illegal or abusive creditor behavior under Iowa’s Consumer Credit Code.
  • Use Iowa-specific exemptions to safeguard your property during negotiations.
  • Help you avoid lawsuits or wage garnishment under Iowa Code § 642.21 with timely legal action.

We don’t just negotiate; we protect your rights every step of the way.

How Our Debt Settlement Process Works

Our process is straightforward, personal, and fully compliant with the law:

  • Detailed Financial Review: In a one-on-one consultation, we review your debts, income, and legal risks. We then identify which debts, such as credit card or medical debts, qualify for settlement and assess whether legal action has already started.
  • Creditor Communication: We handle all communication with creditors, ensuring they follow the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and Iowa’s anti-harassment laws (Iowa Code § 537.7103). This puts an immediate stop to collection calls and threatening letters.
  • Negotiation of Reduced Balances: We work directly with creditors to negotiate reduced balances, either lump sums or structured settlements. Unlike non-legal services, we ensure all agreements are legally enforceable and include liability waivers to protect you.
  • Legal Review of Agreements: We carefully review every settlement agreement to confirm its legality and fairness. We remove improper charges like hidden fees or excessive interest, ensuring your rights are fully protected.
  • Post-Settlement Support: After your settlements are finalized, we monitor the process to confirm creditors’ follow-through. We review your credit reports, address any disputes, and guide you on rebuilding your financial health.

Complete Legal Protection—In or Out of Court

We represent you in court if a creditor files a lawsuit or pursues wage garnishment. Unlike non-attorney services, we can defend you in legal proceedings, respond to garnishment actions, and protect your rights under Iowa law.

Honest Advice, Real Results

Many debt relief companies promise quick fixes but fail to deliver. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we provide honest, realistic advice. We clearly explain your options and risks, helping you decide between debt settlement and other alternatives like Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy. We aim to find the best, most lasting solution for your financial situation.

Debt relief isn’t just about saving money—it’s about restoring your financial stability and peace of mind. With over 50 years of experience serving Iowans from our Dubuque office, we’re here to help you settle your debt with integrity and confidence. Let us guide you toward a brighter financial future.

Take Control of Your Debt Today  

You don’t have to face overwhelming debt alone. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we have over 50 years of experience helping Iowa families find lasting debt relief. Our small, dedicated team listens to your concerns and works with you to create a fresh financial start. We offer solutions like debt negotiation, reorganization, and a full range of Iowa debt relief options.  

The first step toward financial freedom starts with a conversation. Visit our Dubuque office, where we provide a welcoming and supportive environment. Whether you need immediate debt settlement or want to explore all your options for a more stable future, we are here to help. Thousands of Iowans have trusted us to guide them, and now we’re ready to do the same for you.  

Contact Henkels & Baker, PC today to schedule your consultation. We will review your situation, answer your questions, and help you move forward with confidence and peace of mind.

1. What is debt settlement and how does it work in Iowa?

Debt settlement is a process where you negotiate with creditors to pay less than the full amount you owe. Instead of making regular payments to multiple creditors, you or your attorney work to reach an agreement in which the creditor accepts a reduced lump-sum or structured payment to resolve the debt.

  1. When might someone consider debt settlement instead of bankruptcy?

People often consider debt settlement when they are struggling to keep up with unsecured debts like credit cards or medical bills but want to avoid the long-term consequences of filing for bankruptcy. It may be an option when creditors are willing to negotiate and when you have some ability to make a settlement payment.

  1. Will debt settlement stop creditor calls or collection actions?

Once you begin a formal debt settlement process with legal representation, your attorney typically communicates directly with creditors on your behalf. This can reduce or eliminate direct contact from collectors, though there may still be correspondence until settlements are finalized.

  1. How does debt settlement affect my credit score?

Debt settlement can impact your credit score negatively if accounts are reported as “settled” rather than “paid in full.” Over time, however, resolving outstanding debts through settlement may improve your credit profile compared to leaving debts unpaid or allowing collection judgments to stand.

  1. What are the risks or costs associated with debt settlement?

Risks include the possibility that creditors may refuse to settle, that taxes may be owed on forgiven debt, and that your credit score could be damaged. In some cases, interest or fees can accumulate while negotiations are underway. An attorney can help you understand and weigh these potential outcomes.
